title: The Share of a Ridgecrest Advantage Monthly Plan Premium a Subsidised Member Meets
content:
Where a member of a Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan has been awarded a low income premium subsidy, the share of the monthly plan premium the member meets is settled by the low income premium subsidy recorded for that member on their Stand-Alone Medicare Part D Prescription Drug Plans record.

**Full subsidy on that record.** The member meets none of the monthly plan premium, that is 0 per cent of it.

**A seventy-five per cent subsidy on that record.** The member meets a quarter of the monthly plan premium, that is 25 per cent of it.

**A fifty per cent subsidy on that record.** The member meets half of the monthly plan premium, that is 50 per cent of it.

**A twenty-five per cent subsidy on that record.** The member meets three quarters of the monthly plan premium, that is 75 per cent of it.

**No subsidy at all on that record.** The member meets the whole of the monthly plan premium, that is 100 per cent of it.

These five entries are the whole of the ladder, and the drug plan record is the one thing that settles which of them governs. The share the member meets and the subsidy recorded run in opposite directions: the larger the subsidy standing on that record, the smaller the share of the monthly plan premium left to the member, so that a full subsidy leaves nothing to be met and a record showing no subsidy at all leaves all of it.

On a hypothetical monthly plan premium of 80.00 USD for the plan held, the five entries give in turn a plan premium of one coverage month of 0.00 USD, 20.00 USD, 40.00 USD, 60.00 USD and 80.00 USD.
